references.text: Proverbs emphasizes that the one who lives wickedly must bear the consequences of their actions—"they will eat the fruit of their ways." The thief acknowledges that they receive the punishment they deserve for their deeds (Prov 1:31).
Pilate declared that he found no guilt in Jesus. The repentant thief confirms this by stating that Jesus has done nothing wrong (Luke 23:4).

Pilate repeated his assessment that Jesus was innocent, and that neither Herod found any fault in him. The thief's testimony confirms the same truth: "this man has done nothing wrong" (Luke 23:14-15).
For the third time, Pilate declares Jesus' innocence: "I have found no basis for a charge against him that deserves death." The thief's words support this testimony (Luke 23:22).
Peter writes that Christ committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth. The thief's confession points to the same thing: Jesus had done nothing wrong (1 Pet 2:22).

Paul writes that Christ, who knew no sin, was made sin for us. The thief's testimony that Jesus has done nothing wrong points to this truth about the sinless one bearing the punishment of others (2 Cor 5:21).

Isaiah prophesied about the Lord's suffering servant that "he had done no violence, and there was no deceit in his mouth." The thief's acknowledgment of Jesus' innocence fulfills this prophetic word (Isa 53:9).

Peter writes that Christ suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring us to God. The thief acknowledges that he and the other are unrighteous and rightly punished, while Jesus is righteous—precisely the contrast Peter highlights (1 Pet 3:18).
The officer at the cross confirms what the thief said: "This man was truly righteous." Both testify to Jesus' innocence in the midst of his crucifixion (Luke 23:47).
The law prescribed punishment proportional to the crime. The thief acknowledges that he receives just punishment in line with this principle—they get back what they have done (Deut 21:22).
